verdict.rationale: Whether a hosting/deployment platform publishes its source (or that of components such as its CLI) under an open license is a fair openness question for this kind of product, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence pack says any Netlify source is available under an open license. The CLI (netlify-docs-3, netlify-probe-3) and SDK are documented with no licensing information, and the one 'open source' mention (netlify-intdir-11) describes a third-party Svelte framework, not Netlify.
